account:
Today has mostly looked like ordinary town business. I read my appointments, attended morning office hours, and went to the market for my ten o'clock walk. The builder wants agreement on weekly repairs and payment. No defects have yet been confirmed; the builder is inspecting the bridge without spending or altering anything and is to bring an itemized estimate to the one o'clock accounts review. That is an inspection, not evidence of a bridge problem.

The only potentially unusual thread is the bakery. Townsfolk 10 reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the bridge. The secretary also saw the baker near the bridge around ten thirty-six carrying bread, but did not establish the destination or see a companion. My neighbour says neighbours mentioned bakery lights; I have not seen those lights myself or learned when they were seen. According to my neighbour, the baker says fresh bread is coming to market and knows of no special occasion. I recently heard the baker shouting in the distance but could not understand the words.

This could simply be baking and delivery for normal market sales. I do not yet have evidence of a secret gathering, a shortage, or wrongdoing, and cannot tell what the lights were for. The neighbour has noticed no dockside problem, but will look on the way home and tell me what they actually see at our three o'clock tea. Most residents I asked initially had no news. I should distinguish firsthand observations from repeated rumours, learn more about the bakery without making accusations, and keep my remaining appointments.
